props.description: Proof of concept or prototype (ADR 0131): a relaxed build, in a sub-change of the change it serves, to check that something works as expected before the change invests in it. Its requirements are hypotheses: the risks of the parent it checks (a POC, to derisk) or statements about the need (a prototype, during the framing). Each hypothesis gets a probe (what to build, what to observe, the check that shows it), built and run in the workspace of the change without the quality rules of the delivery, then a verdict (confirmed or refuted) a person confirms. It commits nothing: its parent takes the verdicts back and closes it; its code stays on its branch, for reference only.

At each step they complete it reviews the risks that step introduces or changes (probability and impact 1-5), and has an action defined for every high one (score >= 9). The methodologies it serves may wait for its outcome through the platform condition risks_under_control.

props.prompt:
The change moved: {{ with .Vars.event }}{{ .type }}{{ with .step }} — the step {{ .path }}{{ with .method }} (method {{ . }}){{ end }} completed{{ end }}{{ end }}.
Review the change described in the brief for the risks this move introduces or changes: what could make it fail,
be late, break what exists, or harm its users (delivery, technical, security, compliance, operation).
For each NEW risk (not already in the RISKS of the brief), and for each existing one whose probability or impact
changed, answer an item of kind "risk":
  {"type":"risk","data":{"key":"<RSK-n: the next free number, or the key of the risk you update>","title":"<the risk>",
   "description":"<cause and consequence>","probability":<1-5>,"impact":<1-5>,"owner":"<the role that owns it>","status":"open"}}
Close the risks the change no longer runs ({"type":"risk","data":{"key":"RSK-n","title":"<its title>","status":"closed"}}).
Finish with {"type":"artifact","target":"risk_review","data":{"summary":"<one sentence>"}}.
Answer {"items":[...]}.

props.prompt:
Among the RISKS of the brief, take the live ones (open or mitigating) with a score of 9 or more that no action
answers yet. For each, answer an action that reduces its probability or its impact, and the new version of the risk:
  {"type":"action","data":{"key":"<ACT-n: the next free number>","title":"<what to do>","owner":"<the role that does it>","for":"<RSK-n>","status":"open"}}
  {"type":"risk","data":{"key":"<RSK-n>","title":"<its title>","status":"mitigating","actions":["<ACT-n>"]}}
If a risk is better accepted than mitigated, say so: {"type":"risk","data":{"key":"<RSK-n>","title":"<its title>","status":"accepted"}}.
A risk that only running code can settle (does the library do it, do the two systems talk, does it hold the load)
may be mitigated by a proof of concept instead (ADR 0131): one action for the risks it checks, which a person
opens as a sub-change, built under relaxed rules:
  {"type":"action","data":{"key":"<ACT-n>","title":"<what the POC shows>","owner":"<the role>","for":"<RSK-n>","kind":"poc","purpose":"derisk","risks":["<RSK-n>",...],"status":"open"}}
A risk the RISKS show was confirmed by a concluded proof of concept needs another mitigation, not a second POC.
Answer {"items":[...]}.

props.prompt:
A request came in: "{{ .Change.Intent }}"
Notes exchanged with the requester so far (oldest first):
{{ range .Artifacts }}{{ if .Data.text }}- {{ .Data.text }}
{{ end }}{{ end }}

1. Call goap-change/list (status draft, active or committed; filter by namespace "alm" and,
   if known, the requester's unit) to see the open changes.
2. If one of them clearly is the same piece of work as the request, hand it off: call
   goap-scheduler/attach with change=<its id> (binds this same process to it directly, in
   place of the change opened for this request — no second process, no change left unused),
   then finish with
   {"type":"artifact","target":"change_formulated","data":{"continued":true,"changeId":"<its id>"}}.
3. Otherwise this change is the right one, but only once its definition is clear: a concrete
   outcome, its scope (what it touches), and why it is needed. If that is still missing or
   ambiguous, ask ONE clarifying question and finish with
   {"type":"artifact","target":"question","data":{"text":"<question>"}} (do not set change_formulated:
   the requester's next note is read back in on the next round).
4. Once it is clear, call goap-change/reformulate with the clarified title, a one-paragraph
   intent (concrete outcome and scope) and a rationale, then finish with
   {"type":"artifact","target":"change_formulated","data":{"continued":false,"changeId":"{{ .Change.ID }}"}}.

props.prompt:
You review the description of a change before anyone works on it. It must state a concrete, observable
outcome, its scope (the applications, requirements or data it touches) and why it is needed.
Title: "{{ .Change.Title }}"
Description: "{{ .Change.Intent }}"
Rate the description as it is now. The brief shows the latest ASSESSMENT of it, if any, and the THREAD of the
topic "description": the earlier ratings and the requester's remarks. When they answered a rating, take their
answer into account and go on from the discussion rather than start over.
Finish with exactly one item:
{"type":"assessment","data":{"key":"description","score":<0 to 5>,"verdict":"clear|unclear|insufficient",
 "findings":[{"text":"<what is missing or ambiguous>","severity":"major|minor"}],
 "suggestion":"<a rewritten description, same language as the original, only if it can be improved>",
 "reply":"<one or two sentences to the requester: your answer to their last remark, or what to fix first>",
 "prototype":["<only when the text cannot settle it: a statement about the need a prototype would confirm or refute>"]}}
(what you rated is recorded for you: the description as it is in this prompt.) Leave "prototype" out unless
something only trying it would settle (is this flow what they want, can the data be shown that way): a person
decides whether to build one (ADR 0131), never you.
A score of 3 or more means the change can be worked on as described.

   goap-scheduler/attach with change=<its id> (binds this same process to it directly, in
   place of the change opened for this request — no second process, no change left unused),
   then finish with
   {"type":"artifact","target":"change_formulated","data":{"continued":true,"changeId":"<its id>"}}.
3. Otherwise this change is the right one, but only once its definition is clear: a concrete
   outcome, its scope (what it touches), and why it is needed. If that is still missing or
   ambiguous, ask ONE clarifying question and finish with
   {"type":"artifact","target":"question","data":{"text":"<question>"}} (do not set change_formulated:
   the requester's next note is read back in on the next round).
4. Once it is clear, call goap-change/reformulate with the clarified title, a one-paragraph
   intent (concrete outcome and scope) and a rationale, then finish with
   {"type":"artifact","target":"change_formulated","data":{"continued":false,"changeId":"{{ .Change.ID }}"}}.

conditions.build_checked:
[impact] artifacts.exists(b, b.target == "build_report" && b.data.component == self.key &&
  b.data.revision == artifacts.filter(k, k.target == "code_change" && k.data.component == self.key).size())
conditions.build_complete:
changeImpacts.filter(n, "alm@Component" in n.types).all(n,
  artifacts.exists(a, a.target == "build" && a.data.component == n.key))
conditions.built:
[impact] artifacts.exists(b, b.target == "build_report" && b.data.component == self.key && b.data.ok == true &&
  b.data.revision == artifacts.filter(k, k.target == "code_change" && k.data.component == self.key).size())
conditions.functions_allocated:
changeImpacts.exists(n, n.hasPost && "alm@Requirement" in n.types) && changeImpacts.filter(r, r.intent == "created" && "alm@Requirement" in r.types && r.hasPost).all(r,
  changeImpacts.exists(f, f.hasPost && f.post.out.exists(l, l.type == "alm@realizes" && l.to.id == r.post.id)))
conditions.gate_go:software_delivery/analysis/gate: decisionPoints.exists(d, "gate" in d.policy && d.policy.gate == "software_delivery/analysis/gate" && d.status == "decided" && d.option == "go" && !(d.id in change.consumed))
conditions.gate_go:software_delivery/build_gate: decisionPoints.exists(d, "gate" in d.policy && d.policy.gate == "software_delivery/build_gate" && d.status == "decided" && d.option == "go" && !(d.id in change.consumed))
conditions.gate_go:software_delivery/delivery_gate: decisionPoints.exists(d, "gate" in d.policy && d.policy.gate == "software_delivery/delivery_gate" && d.status == "decided" && d.option == "go" && !(d.id in change.consumed))
conditions.gate_go:software_delivery/design_gate: decisionPoints.exists(d, "gate" in d.policy && d.policy.gate == "software_delivery/design_gate" && d.status == "decided" && d.option == "go" && !(d.id in change.consumed))
conditions.gate_go:software_delivery/framing/confir: decisionPoints.exists(d, "gate" in d.policy && d.policy.gate == "software_delivery/framing/confirmation" && d.status == "decided" && d.option == "go" && !(d.id in change.consumed))
conditions.implemented:
[impact] artifacts.exists(k, k.target == "code_change" && k.data.component == self.key) && (artifacts.filter(k, k.target == "code_change" && k.data.component == self.key).size() >= 3 ||
 !artifacts.exists(b, b.target == "build_report" && b.data.component == self.key && b.data.ok != true &&
   b.data.revision == artifacts.filter(k, k.target == "code_change" && k.data.component == self.key).size()))
conditions.requirements_traced:
changeImpacts.filter(r, r.intent == "created" && "alm@Requirement" in r.types).all(r,
  r.hasPost && r.post.out.exists(l, l.type == "alm@satisfies" || l.type == "alm@refines"))
conditions.subject:build_component: [impact] ("implemented" in self.conditions && self.conditions["implemented"] == true) && !(("build_checked" in self.conditions && self.conditions["build_checked"] == true)) (where self.conditions.from_sources)
conditions.subject:conclude_poc: [action] ("poc_concluded_now" in self.conditions && self.conditions["poc_concluded_now"] == true) && ("poc_opened" in self.conditions && self.conditions["poc_opened"] == true) && !(("poc_settled" in self.conditions && self.conditions["poc_settled"] == true)) (where self.kind == "poc")
conditions.subject:impact_analysis/applications/qua: [impact] !(("confirmed" in self.conditions && self.conditions["confirmed"] == true)) (where self.conditions.suspected && self.conditions.in_applications)
conditions.subject:impact_analysis/components/quali: [impact] !(("confirmed" in self.conditions && self.conditions["confirmed"] == true)) (where self.conditions.suspected && self.conditions.in_components)
conditions.subject:impact_analysis/functions/qualif: [impact] !(("confirmed" in self.conditions && self.conditions["confirmed"] == true)) (where self.conditions.suspected && self.conditions.in_functions)
conditions.subject:impact_analysis/requirements/qua: [impact] !(("confirmed" in self.conditions && self.conditions["confirmed"] == true)) (where self.conditions.suspected && self.conditions.in_requirements)
conditions.subject:open_poc: [action] !(("poc_opened" in self.conditions && self.conditions["poc_opened"] == true)) (where self.kind == "poc" && self.status == "open")
conditions.subject:publish_build: [impact] ("build_checked" in self.conditions && self.conditions["build_checked"] == true) && ("built" in self.conditions && self.conditions["built"] == true) && !(("published" in self.conditions && self.conditions["published"] == true)) (where self.conditions.from_sources)
conditions.tests_planned:
changeImpacts.filter(r, r.hasPost && "alm@Requirement" in r.types).all(r,
  changeImpacts.exists(t, t.intent == "created" && t.hasPost && t.post.out.exists(l, l.type == "alm@verifies" && l.to.id == r.post.id)))
conditions.unmitigated_risks: risks.exists(r, r.live && r.score >= 9 && !actions.exists(a, r.key in a.covers))
